verdict.line: You lose if you let him land three hits and start chain-pulling you into stacked Obliterates; you win if you poke from outside 700 range and only transform when his E and R are down.

brief.thesis: Little Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) outranges both Mordekaiser's Q (Obliterate, 675 range) and E (Death's Grasp, 700 range), so the lane is a pure spacing problem, not a damage problem — which is why it's dead even at 50.1% over 1374 games. The moment you transform into Mega Gnar you trade that range for a melee stun kit, which is exactly the fight Mordekaiser wants: his passive Darkness Rise rewards landing three hits, and his W (Indestructible) banks every point of damage exchanged into a shield he can pop to heal. Stay ranged as long as possible; only go Mega Gnar to finish, not to start.

theirWindow.when: his E (Death's Grasp) is off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He can pull you from 700 range into Obliterate and auto range to start stacking Darkness Rise. Do not stand in minion-wave range when his E is up — hold at 1100+ range and only step in to land a Q.

yourWindow.when: his E and R are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is your window to either poke freely with Q/W Hyper autos or transform and all-in with E's earth-shatter plus R's knockback. If you can line him up against a wall for R (GNAR!), the wall-stun and bonus damage end the trade before he can shield-heal.

start.why: 62.6% pick rate and the higher win rate (51.7% over 1080 games) of the two starts — the extra sustain and early AD matter when you're trading autos at range instead of all-in items.

boots.why: 66.7% pick rate at 50% win rate — the magic resist directly blunts Obliterate, Death's Grasp, and the Darkness Rise aura, all magic damage.

core.why: First item in the highest-sample core path (56% over 184 games); the move speed and burst proc help you actually land Q pokes and disengage after.
Second item in all three measured paths — the armor shred and sustained damage matter against his W shield, which banks damage either side deals.
Highest-win-rate third item (56% over 184 games) — the shield and tenacity help you survive the window right before you can disengage from his E pull.

runes.keystoneWhy: Higher sample and win rate than the Lethal Tempo page (51.9% over 35.9% pick vs 49.6% over 25.6% pick) — the sustain and move speed proc reward the poke-and-reposition pattern this lane runs on.

summoners.why: 66.7% pick rate at 50.4% win rate — Teleport lets you reset waves safely after kiting him off, which matters more here than Ignite since this is a spacing lane, not a kill lane.

playing.title: Poke from max Q range
playing.detail: Stay outside 700 range whenever his E is up and throw Q (Boomerang Throw) from distance. Catching the boomerang on return cuts its cooldown, letting you poke again before he can close the gap.

playing.title: Track Death's Grasp, not his HP
playing.detail: His E is the only way he starts a trade on his terms. If it's down, you control distance; if it's up, back off rather than farming the wave edge.

playing.title: Hop to dodge the pull
playing.detail: Use E (Hop) as he casts Death's Grasp — the displacement moves you out of the pull's area before it lands, per OP.GG's own read on this matchup.

playing.title: Build Rage on your terms
playing.detail: Poke with Q and Hyper-empowered autos to fill your Rage gauge in trades you're winning, then transform into Mega Gnar to finish — not as a panic button when he's already on top of you.

playing.title: Never give him three hits
playing.detail: Darkness Rise triggers after 3 landed attacks or spells. Break off a trade after two exchanges rather than trading evenly to a third, since the aura and move speed kick in right after.

playing.title: Save R for a wall
playing.detail: GNAR! (R) stuns and deals bonus damage to anyone thrown into a wall. Hold the ultimate until you can force him against terrain instead of using it in open lane.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting him head on, while using [E] to dodge his (E). Kite him while keeping your distance to gain the upper hand.
